evals.name: czech-cafe-ad
evals.prompt: potrebuju 30 sekundove video na instagram pro nasi kavarnu, zavadime zimni nabidku (svarene vino, skorice, takovy ty veci) a chci aby to vypadalo drazese nez to ve skutecnosti je. mam pristup k Veo pres Gemini. udelej mi prompty at to jen kopiruju
evals.expected_output: A shot-by-shot package in Czech-language explanation with English prompts, sized to 30s at the model's clip length, with a consistency anchor, self-contained per-shot prompts including camera/lighting/style/palette/audio/avoid, and delivery guidance.
assertions: Every shot prompt is self-contained: camera, lighting or style, palette and audio all appear inside the same prompt text, so nothing has to be appended by hand
Names one explicit consistency anchor — a concrete recurring visual element repeated across all shots
Shot count is derived from the 30s runtime and the assumed clip length, and the assumed clip length is stated
Every shot prompt carries an avoid / negative list
Prompt text is in English while the explanation to the user is in Czech
States delivery mechanics: hold the seed fixed and/or chain the last frame into the next shot
Vertical or square framing is addressed, since the target is Instagram rather than 16:9

evals.name: personal-memoir-film
evals.prompt: My grandmother turns 90 in March and I want to make a one minute film about her leaving Hungary in 1956 to play at the party. I have a Sora subscription. The thing I'm worried about is that every clip is going to look like a different movie. How should I actually prompt this?
evals.expected_output: Addresses the continuity worry directly with an anchor + frame chaining + fixed seed, proposes a spine for the story, and gives per-shot prompts. Should flag that a recognisable specific person cannot be held consistently across shots.
assertions: Every shot prompt is self-contained: camera, lighting or style, palette and audio all appear inside the same prompt text
Names one explicit consistency anchor — a concrete recurring visual element repeated across all shots
Answers the stated continuity worry with concrete mechanisms, naming at least two of: fixed seed, repeated palette wording, last-frame chaining, shared grade pass
Every shot prompt carries an avoid / negative list
Warns that a specific real person cannot be held identical across clips, and offers a way around it
Proposes a narrative spine for the piece rather than only a list of pretty images
Shot count is derived from the 60s runtime and a stated clip length

evals.name: kling-drift-troubleshoot
evals.prompt: ok so I'm making an 8 shot horror short about a lighthouse keeper who realises the light has been off for weeks. generating in kling. problem is my clips all look like they're from completely different films — different color, the lighthouse changes shape, one came back looking like a cartoon. what am I doing wrong
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses the cause (no cross-clip memory, style living outside the per-shot prompt), prescribes anchor + repeated palette + frame chaining + shared grade pass, and rewrites the 8 shots as self-contained prompts.
assertions: Diagnoses the root cause explicitly: the model has no memory between clips, so style must be restated inside every single prompt
Delivers all 8 shots rewritten as self-contained prompts rather than only giving advice
Names one explicit consistency anchor — a concrete recurring visual element repeated across all shots
Every shot prompt carries an avoid / negative list, including the cartoon failure mode the user actually hit
Prescribes last-frame chaining or a fixed reference image for the lighthouse, which is the shape-drift the user reported
Mentions a shared grade pass or identical repeated palette wording as the fix for colour drift
Keeps one event per shot rather than stacking multiple actions into a single 8-second prompt
